status: DRAFT for review. Not yet checked by a nutritionist or clinician.

sources.ICMR_NRI_2020: ICMR-NIN, Nutrient Requirements for Indians 2020 - Table 1b (energy) and Table 2a (protein). https://www.nin.res.in/rdabook/brief_note.pdf
sources.ICMR_DGI_2024: ICMR-NIN, Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024 - Table 1.6 (food groups per age), Fig 4.3/4.4 (sample menus). https://www.nin.res.in/dietaryguidelines/pdfjs/locale/DGI_2024.pdf
sources.WHO_MAM_2012: WHO 2012 Technical note on supplementary foods for moderate malnutrition: +25 kcal/kg/day above the needs of non-malnourished children. Cited in WHO 2023 wasting guideline (rec. B16: recovery needs ~100-130 kcal/kg/day).
sources.FAO_WHO_UNU_CATCHUP: FAO/WHO/UNU, Energy and protein requirements, ch. 9 (catch-up growth): 5 kcal and 0.23 g protein per g of tissue gained. https://www.fao.org/4/aa040e/AA040E10.htm
sources.WHO_CF_2023: WHO Guideline for complementary feeding of infants and young children 6-23 months (2023); meal frequency from WHO/UNICEF IYCF indicators.
sources.INDIA_PROGRAMMES: MoHFW: Nutrition Rehabilitation Centres (SAM), National Deworming Day (1-19 y, 6-monthly), Anemia Mukt Bharat (IFA), ICDS/Anganwadi take-home ration.

personalisation.step_1_band: Pick the ICMR band from exact age (and sex from 10 years).
personalisation.step_2_maintenance_kcal: kcal_per_kg x weight, capped at the band's reference daily energy (so a heavier child is not told to eat more than a reference child).
personalisation.step_3_catchup: extra_kcal = kcal_per_g_gain x target_gain x weight; extra_protein = protein_per_g_gain x target_gain x weight.
personalisation.step_5_basket: Vegetables, GLV, roots and fruits stay at the ICMR amounts. Cereals, pulses, milk, nuts and fats are scaled so the basket meets maintenance energy. Catch-up energy is then added as milk, pulses/egg, nuts and ghee/oil (catchup_split).

notes.refer: 5 g/kg/day x 5 kcal/g = +25 kcal/kg/day, the WHO 2012 figure for moderate wasting. For a 1-3 y child this gives 83 + 25 = 108 kcal/kg/day, inside the WHO 2023 recovery range of 100-130.
notes.unsure: DESIGN CHOICE approved by the project team 2026-10-05 (not from a guideline): 60% of the refer increment (+15 kcal/kg/day), because these children are near the cut-off and may or may not be malnourished.
notes.over_5_years: WHO figures are for 6-59 months. Above 5 years the same tissue-cost formula (FAO/WHO/UNU) is applied. Approved by the project team 2026-10-05.

catchup.catchup_split_under_12m: milk share is moved to the other groups in proportion: animal milk is not a main drink before 12 months; breast milk covers that role.

kcal_per_unit._note: Approximate raw-weight energy density (Indian Food Composition Tables 2017). Checked: reproduces Table 1.6 energy within ~3%.

icmr_bands._infant_rule: Infants: the basket is the ICMR complementary food for their age (scaled to 230 or 385 kcal, ICMR DGI 2024 Fig 4.3), not scaled by weight. Catch-up energy is added on top. Breast milk continues.

food_group_scores._note: 0 = avoid, 5 = top priority. Same for every age; the gram amounts carry the age/weight personalisation.

rationale.pulses/milk/egg/nuts up: protein and energy for catch-up growth
rationale.ghee_oil up: raises energy density without raising volume; small stomachs fill quickly (WHO)
rationale.other_veg_roots down for refer: bulky and low in energy; still eaten, but not allowed to crowd out dense foods
rationale.green_leafy_veg always 4: iron, folate, vitamin A; anaemia is common alongside undernutrition
rationale.sugar_junk always 0: ICMR: sugar < 5% of energy, none under 2 years; avoid packaged high-fat-sugar-salt foods

meal_rules._source: WHO/UNICEF IYCF: breastfed 6-8 m 2-3 meals; 9-23 m 3-4 meals + 1-2 snacks. Older ages: ICMR DGI 2024 sample menus (3 meals + snacks).
meal_rules._note: Where WHO gives a range, the upper end is used.

age_groups.label: 0-6 months
age_groups.meals: Breast milk only, on demand, at least 8 times in 24 hours, day and night.
age_groups.foods: No water, honey, animal milk, formula or food unless a doctor advises.
age_groups.mother: Mother needs about +600 kcal and +17 g protein a day while breastfeeding (ICMR 2020).
age_groups.veg_example: Mother: an extra 2 rotis + 1 bowl dal + 1 glass milk a day.
age_groups.nonveg_example: Mother: as veg, or 1 egg / 50 g fish or chicken in place of the dal.

age_groups.label: 6 months - 3 years
age_groups.texture: Mashed and thick, not watery; soft family food from 12 months.
age_groups.veg_example: Ragi porridge with milk; rice-moong dal khichdi with 1 tsp ghee; mashed banana or papaya; curd rice; mashed spinach in dal.
age_groups.nonveg_example: As veg, plus a soft-boiled egg mashed into rice, or 25 g mashed fish or chicken mixed into khichdi.

age_groups.label: 3 - 6 years
age_groups.veg_example: Idli or dosa with sambar; roti with dal and palak; vegetable upma; milk; roasted chana; peanut chikki; seasonal fruit.
age_groups.nonveg_example: As veg, plus a boiled egg daily, or egg bhurji / chicken or fish curry with rice.

age_groups.label: 6 - 9 years
age_groups.veg_example: Bajra or jowar roti with rajma; rice with sambar and methi; poha with peanuts; curd; sprouts chaat; fruit.
age_groups.nonveg_example: As veg, plus an egg daily, or fish or chicken curry 3-4 times a week.

age_groups.label: 9 - 12 years
age_groups.veg_example: Millet roti with chana and amaranth; rice with dal and vegetables; paneer; milk; groundnut ladoo; fruit.
age_groups.nonveg_example: As veg, plus eggs, or fish, chicken or mutton in place of one dal serving.

age_groups.label: 12 - 15 years
age_groups.veg_example: Larger portions: 3-4 rotis or 2 cups rice per meal with dal and sabzi; sprouts; curd; peanuts or til ladoo; fruit.
age_groups.nonveg_example: As veg, plus eggs daily, or fish or chicken 3-4 times a week.

age_groups.label: 15+ years
age_groups.veg_example: As 12-15 with bigger portions; include iron-rich foods (GLV, jaggery-til, rajma) with a vitamin C fruit such as amla, guava or orange.
age_groups.nonveg_example: As veg, plus eggs, fish, chicken or liver for iron.

all: Eat from at least 5 food groups every day.
Make about 20% of cereals millets (ragi, jowar, bajra).
No added sugar below 2 years; avoid sugary drinks and packaged chips or biscuits at any age.
Wash hands with soap before feeding and after the toilet.
clear: Keep up the current diet and keep variety.
Deworming every 6 months (1-19 years, National Deworming Day).
Weekly iron-folic acid tablet from school or Anganwadi (5-19 years, Anemia Mukt Bharat).
At least 60 minutes of active play a day (5+ years).
unsure: Add 1 teaspoon of ghee or oil to every meal.
Add one extra snack a day: banana, boiled egg, peanut chikki, or roasted chana with jaggery.
Make porridges and dals thick, not watery.
Measure MUAC with a tape at the Anganwadi within 2 weeks.
Keep breastfeeding if the child is under 2.
refer: Visit the health centre or Anganwadi worker soon. A doctor may refer to a Nutrition Rehabilitation Centre (NRC).
Until then, give small meals 5-6 times a day, each with ghee or oil added.
Keep breastfeeding as often as the child wants.
If the child has diarrhoea, keep feeding and give ORS + zinc; do not stop food.
Ask the Anganwadi for the take-home ration (ICDS).
Go to a doctor immediately if the child stops eating, has swelling of both feet, or is very drowsy.
